messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] prod-eu inference queue length = 12,800; 95th token latency spiked to 3.2s; error rate +18%. Autoscaler attempted provisioning but reports failures. Paging oncall.
ryan: oncall (ryan) - ACK. I'm pulling logs and checking autoscaler.
maria: seeing lots of `quotaExceeded` in cloud API for GPUs around 02:14 UTC. Autoscaler hit project GPU quota ceiling, refused new nodes.
sanjay: also seeing scheduling failures: pods pending with reason `Insufficient GPU` and many nodes partially occupied by small-MIG slices. binpacking failing due to fragmentation.
linh: customer-impact: CS reports multiple timeouts from AcmePay and HealthMap; sessions getting 504s. Ticket IDs: CS-4312, CS-4313.
ryan: copying logs ->
```
I0402 02:14:03 kube-scheduler PodBinding failed: Insufficient resources: nvidia.com/gpu
autoscaler: scaleUp failed: quotas.gcp.com error=quotaExceeded, requested 4 gpus, available 0
```
ryan: quick plan: 1) try soft mitigation (enable fallback model + routing), 2) offload some heavy workloads to dedicated-pool, 3) request emergency GPU quota bump with cloud.
maria: i'm 2nd on quota request with cloud support ticket 0-CC-9982, ETA unknown. In the meantime we can: reduce replica counts for large models, enable caching, and switch some customers to smaller variants.
sanjay: fragmentation details — many nodes are GP100-sized nodes with heterogeneous MIG slices: a lot of 1g.5 profile slices and some 7g.40. New pods request 2g slices so they can't fit. There's ~16 nodes with stranded 1-2 GPU-equivalents unusable for current pod shapes.
nicole: ops-bot, any automated rebin/evac tools?
ops-bot: auto-rebalance attempted at 02:10 UTC but skipped 9 nodes due to live pods with evictionProtection label. Manual intervention required.
linh: can we temporarily scale down background batch jobs and free up whole GPUs? Many batch jobs run in prod-eu batch namespace.
ryan: good call. I'm going to patch batch jobs to `replicas: 0` for the heaviest ones.
ryan: running:
```
kubectl -n batch deploy heavy-encoder-pool scale --replicas=0
kubectl -n batch deploy offline-embedder scale --replicas=0
```
ryan: patched 3 deployments, freed ~6 GPUs (but fragmentation still prevents optimal packing).
sanjay: we need to change MIG sizing or move workloads to differently shaped nodes. Short term: create a few new node pools with full-GPU (no-MIG) to accept 2g requests. But cloud quota is zero -> can't.
maria: alternative: lower pod `resources.requests.gpu` for non-critical models to use 1g slices, then increase parallelism per pod. Risk: slightly slower per-request throughput, but will unstick queue. Thoughts?
icole: from CS side, we can triage customers: move top 3 paying customers to dedicated-pool (we have reserved capacity there). That should reduce external customer impact quickly.
linh: initiating move for AcmePay to dedicated-pool via routing rules. @nicole I sent them note about planned temporary move.
linh: routing change: 10.2.0.0/24 -> dedicated-pool, applied.
ops-bot: routing change deployed; 8% of prod-eu traffic now to dedicated-pool.
ryan: enabling lighter fallback model (llama-7b-quant) for public traffic to reduce GPU usage. Deploying feature-flag switch.
```
PATCH /api/v1/route/prod-eu
{ "fallback_model": "llama-7b-quant", "pct": 100 }
```
ryan: fallback deployed to 100% for standard plans, enterprise still pinned.
linh: after routing/fallback, queue dropped from 12.8k -> 4.2k over 8 minutes. Error rate down to +6%. Latency 95th down to 1.1s.
maria: cloud support responded: they can fast-track quota bump of +32 GPUs but need approval and org admin. 
sanjay: long term fixes we should track in the incident: 1) normalize MIG profiles so scheduling can binpack, 2) change default pod request shapes to be more packable, 3) add autoscaler fallback to create no-MIG pools when fragmentation prevents placement, 4) improve preemption for batch workloads.
nicole: CS requested a short customer impact summary we can share with accounts in 30m.
ryan: drafting impact blurb: "Between 02:10 and 02:45 UTC prod-eu experienced degraded inference throughput due to GPU allocation failures caused by a combination of provider quota exhaustion and heterogeneous MIG sizing, leading to a backlog and increased timeouts for some customers. Mitigations included routing top customers to dedicated capacity, enabling a quantized fallback model, and scaling down non-critical batch jobs. Immediate reduction in error rate and latency observed. Postmortem and remediation plan to follow."
linh: oncall handoff: I'm online for next 90 mins then will hand to sanjay.
sanjay: taking over at 03:00 UTC. I'll coordinate quota bump and raft of infra changes.
ops-bot: incident declared Sev2 by ryan at 02:28 UTC. Runbook: start incident page and notify ENG-SRE, PRODUCT, CS.
nicole: notifying accounts teams and affected customers. Drafted message for AcmePay and HealthMap; waiting for final signoff.
ryan: next actions captured: - follow cloud quota ticket - schedule emergency change to unify MIG sizes in prod-eu - add autoscaler fallback policy - run postmortem. Owners: maria (quota/Cloud comms), sanjay (repack + MIG plan), ryan (postmortem lead), nicole (customer comms).
linh: any objections to labeling this one as 'stranded-gpu-binpack' for tracking?
sanjay: +1.
ryan: closing thread for now; continue updates on the incident page. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
